steps.title: The braai
steps.body: In South Africa, Pinotage is the wine of the braai, the national barbecue: sausages, called boerewors, lamb chops and steak. Its smoky, fruity side suits charred meat and spicy sauces. It also goes with bobotie, a lightly spiced Cape Malay minced meat dish.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 15 to 17 degrees; fruity styles can be slightly cooler. Most Pinotage is best within five years. Old-vine, structured examples can age 10 to 15 years, gaining earthy, savoury notes. Rosé Pinotage is best young and chilled.

steps.prompt: Which dish is a classic South African partner for Pinotage?
steps.explanation: Smoky grilled sausage suits Pinotage's fruit and smoke.

steps.body: Coffee-style Pinotage is a fun match for barbecue ribs with a sweet, smoky glaze. Its mocha notes echo the char.

steps.prompt: Most Pinotage is made for long ageing of 20 years or more.
steps.explanation: Not true. Most is best within five years; only top examples age 10 to 15 years.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Pinotage suits the braai and bobotie
Most is best young; old-vine wines age 10 to 15 years
